title: Introduce observability rationale API and token-penalty meter
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Added a read-only Rationale API for alert explanations and a lightweight token-penalty meter used by alert scoring. No customer-facing API changes. Backfilled dashboards and tuned a set of alert rules.
description: Context: On-call and SREs increasingly ask not just that an SLO is breached, but why — which token phases, model variants, or kernel queues contributed to the cost/latency signal. This PR implements a focused observability surface: (1) a read-only 'rationale' API that returns a concise, machine- and human-readable explanation for an alert window (token phase breakdowns, top-3 contributing callsites, and suggested mitigation), and (2) a new token-penalty meter used to weight samples for the alerting engine so that alerts reflect cost-incurring tokens rather than raw invocation counts. Motivation: reduce alert noise and speed up RCA by surface-level explainability without requiring deep trace pulls or heavy-weight queries. Summary of changes: - telemetry/service/rationale_api.py: new lightweight HTTP handler (read-only) that accepts alert_id/window and returns a compact rationale object (phase_summaries, contributors, suggested_fallbacks). Includes endpoint auth via existing service token. - telemetry/penalty/token_penalty.py: token-penalty meter implementation (pluggable strategy interface + default strategy combining token_cost, kernel_backpressure_factor, and kv_cache_miss_weight). - infra/alerts/alert_rules.yml: updated rule templates to call the penalty-weighted rate and include rationale links in alert messages. - console/dashboards/rationale-panel.json: added a small explainer panel and a sparkline that breaks tokens by phase for the selected window; the panel uses the rationale API for on-demand enrichment. - sdk-python/redwood/observability.py: thin client helper to call the rationale API and render results for internal CLI tooling and runbooks. - tests/*: unit tests for penalty scoring, rationale summarizer, and end-to-end smoke test that runs against the staging telemetry stack. - docs/observability/rationale-api.md: usage, examples, and recommended alert message templates. Migration/rollout plan: 1) Deploy rationale API behind a feature flag in staging and enable the console panel for internal users. 2) Use the penalty meter in a passive mode (adds a tag to alerts but doesn't change routing) for 48h to compare signal. 3) Flip penalty weighting into active alert scoring and watch SRE dashboards for false-negatives/positives. Monitoring and safeguards: - The rationale API is intentionally rate-limited and caches computed rationales for 15 minutes to avoid heavy query load. - Added a cost-safety circuit: if the rationale generation backend detects a query would scan >1M tokens, it returns a summarized fallback and records a telemetry event. - Penalty meter is configurable per-tenant and defaults to conservative weights (cost x1.0, backpressure x0.5, miss x1.2). Testing: - Unit tests: penalty math, serialization of rationale. - Integration: simulated alert windows with synthetic traces to validate the top-3 contributor extraction. - Load test: generated 500 concurrent rationale requests hitting cached vs. uncached paths; no P95 latency regression seen in staging. Rollback: feature flags and per-tenant gates allow immediate disable. Related work: ENG-4021 (alert explainability roadmap), ENG-4120 (token-cost-weighting for SLOs). Checklist: - [x] Implementation complete - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Dashboard panel added - [x] Docs and runbook snippets - [x] Feature flags and conservative default weights - [x] Verified basic load behavior in staging

review_comments: Diego Mendez (review): The rationale payload looks good but we should make sure we never include PII from logs. Please confirm scrub steps and add a test.
Author (Asha): Added a scrubber to the summarizer and a unit test in tests/test_rationale.py that verifies no raw log snippets are emitted. See commit b2c3d4e.
Priya Singh (review): Token penalty math is intuitive, but suggest exposing an orthogonal per-model multiplier so we can tune for heavy vs light models. Also add a brief note in docs.
Author (Asha): Exposed model_multiplier as a config knob; default 1.0. Updated docs with tuning guidance.
Liam O'Connor (approval): Verified integration test and staging load. Recommend squash+merge once CI passes.
notes: This PR focuses on developer and SRE tooling; it intentionally keeps the rationale API read-only and limited to internal tokens. We should consider extending the rationale model to include suggested automated mitigations in a follow-up (ENG-4204).
